subject: Re: Private deployment — custody, operator access & cross-border BYOK questions

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmebio.com>

Subject: Private deploy BYOK — escrow & operator access follow-up

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re progressing internal approvals for a private deployment (VPC-hosted customer control plane) and have a few open items from security and procurement:

- Escrow: our security team expects a clear description of any key escrow process for customer keys (if applicable) and whether Redwood would retain any copy of CMKs or unwrapped keys.
- Operator access: we need the operational playbook for break-glass and forensic access — who can access plaintext (if anyone), what approvals are required, and how long sessions are logged/retained.
- Subprocessors and cross-border transfers: a CSV of subprocessors used in private deployments (including monitoring/telemetry vendors) and an explanation of whether any telemetry leaves customer-controlled VPCs.
- DPA redlines: legal provided a few redlines around data transfers and subprocessors; attached is a short list.

Can you please confirm whether Redwood can do a BYOK model where (a) customer controls CMKs in their KMS, (b) Redwood operates without holding key material, and (c) in a break-glass Redwood uses an auditable, time-limited mechanism that requires customer approval? If that last part isn’t possible, what alternatives do you offer (escrow, escrow + dual-control, or on-site operator assistance)?

Appreciate a concise answer/plan so we can move to procurement.

Cheers,
Sam
Security Ops, Acme Biotech
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmebio.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy BYOK — escrow & operator access follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya / Acme legal,

Thanks — quick summary up front then a couple internal asks. Short answer: yes, we support a BYOK model for Private Deployments where the customer retains sole custody of unwrapped CMKs. We do not persist plaintext keys in Redwood-managed storage for the default private deployment configuration. Details below and attached is our "privdep-kms-handshake" doc with diagrams.

High level:
- BYOK & custody: Customers can bring their CMKs (Cloud KMS or HSM-backed). Redwood can be configured to use the customer's KMS without storing unwrapped keys. For on-prem installs the local KMS/HSM remains the source of truth.
- Escrow: We generally do not require escrow as a default; however, for some regulated customers we offer an optional dual-control escrow where an encrypted key envelope is held in an escrow KMS requiring two parties to reconstruct (customer + Redwood). This is an optional add-on and requires contract-level acceptance.
- Operator break-glass: Our standard offering is that Redwood engineers have no persistent ability to decrypt customer workloads. For break-glass we offer an auditable process:
  * Customer raises a support case and must provide pre-authorized break-glass token (per contract).
  * Access is time-limited (SC-approved window), recorded with session recordings and keystroke logs where allowed, and requires at least two internal approvals (on-call + security manager).
  * All break-glass events generate an immutable audit bundle (telemetry, stack trace, actions) delivered to customer and retained per DPA retention schedule.
- Telemetry & subprocessors: For VPC private deployments we surface an explicit list of subprocessors engaged for monitoring (agent vendor, metrics backend). Telemetry collected by Redwood for observability is configurable and can be restricted to non-PHI usage; sensitive telemetry can be routed to customer-owned endpoints. See attached subprocessors CSV.

Internal note: Rishi — do we have any customers with a required escrow workflow that demanded offline key release? If yes, can you add a one-paragraph precedent we can share?

Sam — I’ve attached the DPA extract you sent with a few inline comments. Happy to jump on a call to walk legal through the process. If you’d like a more conservative contract language we can propose the escrow + dual-control addendum.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deploy BYOK — custody, operator access & cross-border BYOK questions

Sam / Priya / Acme legal — thanks for the patience. Quick, concrete answers below and attached templates.

1) Escrow models (we support three options):
   - No escrow (default): Redwood never stores unwrapped keys; customer KMS is the sole source of crypto operations.
   - Encrypted envelope escrow (optional add-on): Redwood stores an encrypted key envelope that cannot be used alone; reconstruction requires customer-held key + Redwood-held shard (dual-control). This requires an addendum and SOW.
   - Physical HSM escrow (regulated deployments): escrowing a wrapped key in a hardware module under strict custody rules; used for some on-prem or air-gapped customers.

2) Operator break-glass (engineered flow):
   - Pre-authorized token: customer provides a pre-authorized per-incident token (time-limited) or a per-case signed request from an authorized customer admin.
   - Redwood approvals: access requires 2 internal approvers (on-call engineer + security lead), time-limited steward session (default 2 hours, extendable with customer re-approval).
   - Audit: full session capture, command logs, and an immutable audit bundle are produced and delivered to the customer within 24 hours. Logs retained per contract (default 1 year; negotiable).

3) Telemetry & subprocessors:
   - Default telemetry: metrics and health pings are configurable. For VPC Private Deploy we can route metrics/traces to customer endpoints; by default lightweight heartbeat metrics are sent to Redwood-managed endpoints for fleet health.
   - Subprocessors: attached CSV lists agent vendor, metrics backend, incident-response partner. No telemetry leaves the customer VPC if customer selects "customer-owned sink" during deployment. We will notify customers of any new subprocessors 30 days in advance and offer mitigations.

4) DPA redlines & contract language (copyable bullets):
   - "Redwood will not persist unwrapped customer master keys in Redwood-managed storage for Private Deployments in customer VPCs. Any optional escrow arrangement will be documented via an addendum specifying dual-control reconstruction procedures."
   - "Break-glass access requires a pre-authorized token or signed customer approval, two Redwood approvers, session duration cap, and delivery of a complete immutable audit bundle to the customer within 24 hours."

Attachments: escrow-addendum-template.pdf, subprocessors-20260517.csv, privdep-kms-handshake-v1.pdf

If this looks good I can have legal produce the addendum and a short SOW for escrow pricing.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Applied ML & Security, Redwood Inference
